rows.evidence: Q1: Methods - three-year (2013-2016) replicated plot experiment (4 treatments x 3 replicates) in a greenhouse cucumber-celery rotation in Beijing, NCP. Q2: Table 3 and Results 'Vegetable yields, NUE and IWUE' - RFPD (drip fertigation + 40% less urea-N) gave mean annual cucumber yield of 100 t/ha vs 96 for FP and celery 97 vs 94 (celery significantly higher), with text stating reducing synthetic N by 40% under drip had no negative impact on yields; Table 4 NUE +25% and IWUE +40% for RFPD vs FP; Table 2 N2O reduced 45%. Q8: 'Study limitation and future perspectives' - only one fruit-leafy cropping pattern at one NCP site, application at regional/national scale needs multi-year verification of other patterns; yield gap only appeared from S4 due to high initial soil organic matter and NO3-, so recommended N rate depends on initial soil N; other N loss pathways not measured. Q9: Table 3 - yields given as means of three replicates with standard errors.
rows.notes: Yield measured only by harvest weighing (one method). Study measured WFPS and soil mineral N, but these were analysed against N2O fluxes, not as the pathway to yield; yield mechanism (drip meeting plant N and water needs) is inferred, so Q4 'no'. Only one site/soil and two crops (Q5 no); 8 m x 6 m plots (Q6 no). Authors note initial soil N content should be considered when setting the reduced N rate, but do not state it as a requirement for the yield effect (Q7 no, borderline). The passage's 'significantly improved yield' overstates: cucumber yield under RFPD was not significantly different from FP (100ab vs 96b); only celery was significantly higher; authors describe yield as 'maintained'. RFPD confounds drip with reduced N, but the passage names the combination.

rows.evidence: Q1: Methods - three-year replicated greenhouse plot experiment in Beijing, NCP. Q2: Table 1 - drip treatments received 20-40% less irrigation water per season (e.g. 4190 vs 5200 m3/ha, S1); Table 4 and Results - IWUE of FPD and RFPD significantly higher than FP in every season, mean annual IWUE increased by 37% (FPD) and 40% (RFPD); irrigation volume recorded by water meter. Q8: 'Study limitation and future perspectives' - single cropping pattern at one NCP site, larger-scale application needs multi-year verification, other N loss pathways unknown.
rows.notes: IWUE computed as yield/irrigation amount from a single method (metered water and harvest weights); no triangulation. No intermediate variable for water saving (e.g. soil evaporation, drainage/percolation) measured; WFPS was measured but used for N2O analysis (Q4 no). One site, one soil, two crops (Q5 no); plot scale (Q6 no). No condition stated as required for the IWUE gain (Q7 no). Table 4 gives IWUE only as means with letter groupings, no SE or CI (Q9 no).

rows.evidence: Q1: Methods - three-year replicated greenhouse plot experiment, Beijing. Q2: Abstract and Table 4 - RFPD (drip fertigation with 40% less urea-N) mitigated area- and yield-scaled N2O by about 45%, improved IWUE by 40% and NUE by 25% vs FP while maintaining yield; Table 1 shows reduced irrigation amounts under drip; Table 3 celery yield 97 vs 94 t/ha. Q8: 'Study limitation and future perspectives' - only one cropping pattern at one NCP site, regional/national application needs verification, other N losses not quantified.
rows.notes: Numbers in the passage match the abstract. IWUE from a single method (water meter + harvest); no second independent method. No water-balance intermediate (evaporation, percolation) measured (Q4 no). Single site/soil, two crops (Q5 no); plot scale (Q6 no). No stated requirement for the IWUE effect (Q7 no). IWUE in Table 4 reported without dispersion measures (Q9 no); N2O and yield have SE but the rated function is water conservation.

rows.evidence: Q1: Methods - three-year replicated greenhouse plot experiment in Beijing, NCP. Q2: Table 3 and Results - RFPD significantly enhanced mean annual celery yield (97 vs 94 t/ha for FP) and cucumber yield not reduced (100 vs 96); text states 40% synthetic-N reduction under drip had no negative impact on cucumber and celery yields; Table 4 NUE +25%, IWUE +40%; Table 2 N2O -45%. Q8: 'Study limitation and future perspectives' - single cropping pattern at one site, larger-scale validity needs verification; yield gap in unfertilized plots appeared only from S4 due to high initial soil N, so recommended N rate must consider initial soil N; further verification needed for more severe N reduction. Q9: Table 3 - yields as means of three replicates with standard errors.
rows.notes: Yield by harvest weighing only (Q3 no). Soil WFPS and mineral N were measured but analysed as drivers of N2O, not as the pathway to yield (Q4 no, borderline). One site/soil, two crops (Q5 no); plots 8 x 6 m (Q6 no). Authors flag initial soil N content as something to account for, not as a stated requirement for maintained yield (Q7 no). Celery yield under RFPD was actually significantly higher in mean annual terms, consistent with 'maintaining'. Effect is of drip fertigation combined with N reduction, as the passage states.

notes: Full text available and complete. Primary three-year plot experiment at a single greenhouse site in the North China Plain (cucumber-celery rotation, silt loam Cambisol). Drip is applied as drip fertigation; FPD vs FP isolates the drip effect while RFPD combines drip with 40% synthetic-N reduction, which is what the passages describe. N2O, yield and IWUE each measured by one method; SE given for N2O and yield (Tables 2-3) but not for IWUE/NUE (Table 4).
